Boss warnings, run records with personal bests, and pointers to downed party members.

## New

- **Boss warnings:** the last 10 seconds before each boss show as a big countdown over your hero, with the boss's name (red, or gold for the final boss) and the raid-warning sound as it starts. A boss that turns enraged flashes ENRAGED for a moment.
- **Run records:** when a run ends, a record opens with the result and 12 numbers: time, level, kills, damage per second, damage, gold, bosses, elites, guardians, caches, damage taken and magnets. Under each is your best for that zone and class, or a gold **NEW BEST** where you beat it. Time counts the fastest win, or in a run you lost, the longest you lasted. Your last 30 runs are listed on the right. `/aether runs` opens it any time.
- **Downed allies (co-op):** when a party member goes down, a plate names them with how far they are (in reach, close, in sight, far) or how far along your revive is. A pulsing red gem on the minimap's ring and a small compass on their party frame point to where they lie (north-up, like the minimap).
- `/aether` has two more switches: the boss-warning sound, and whether the run record opens by itself when a run ends. There's also a **Run records** button.

## Notes

- Bests are kept per zone and class (endless runs separately), shared by every hero on your account, and saved when you leave the world.
- Every new part can be switched off in `/aether`, and moved with `/aether unlock`.

## Install

1. Download `AetherHUD.zip` below.
2. Delete the old `AetherHUD` folder from `benilla-config/AddOns/`, then unzip the new one there, so you end up with `benilla-config/AddOns/AetherHUD/AetherHUD.toc`.
   **Browser:** Options → AddOns → install the zip.

Your settings and frame positions carry over.

An Aion-style UI for Azeroth Survivors. It replaces the whole interface: the run HUD, your frames, bags, character window, chat, minimap and the pop-up text, in navy glass panels with gold trim and aether-blue glow.

![A run in Elwynn Forest with AetherHUD](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NORehabRocket/AetherHUD/main/docs/screenshots/run.webp)

## What's in it

- Run clock with a boss timeline and next-boss countdown
- Boss bars with an enrage glow and debuff timers (click a bar to target)
- Enemy health plates and floating combat numbers (crits in gold)
- Hero, target, party and pet frames
- Skill bar with cooldowns, rank gems and talent/jewelry timers
- Inventory, plus a character window with every run stat and what your gear adds
- Winged banners, loot cards, system messages and a low-health glow
- Combat meter (damage, healing, boss, taken), run tally and lair tracker
- Glass chat, ring minimap, tooltips and menus

## Install

1. Download `AetherHUD.zip` below.
2. **Windows / Linux:** unzip into `benilla-config/AddOns/` next to `AzerothSurvivors.exe`, so you end up with `benilla-config/AddOns/AetherHUD/AetherHUD.toc`.
   **Browser:** Options → AddOns → install the zip.
3. Turn off other full UIs (PhantomUI, SurvivorsDragonUi).

## Commands

`/aether` options · `/aether unlock` move and resize frames · `/aether demo` preview outside a run · `/aether reset` default layout

## Good to know

- Every part can be switched off on its own, and the game's own HUD comes back when you log out or remove the addon.
- The game's build row (spells + jewelry) stays, because addons can't read jewelry. Hide it in `/aether` if the skill bar is enough for you.
- The talent window, world map and NPC windows are still the game's own.
- This is a beta. Please report bugs with a screenshot in the Issues tab.

### Release v2.6.7-azs
- **Hotfix for Core.lua Tick Update Call**:
  - Implemented `mod:Update(state)` in `Pins.lua` forwarding to `mod:UpdateRadar()`.
  - Added defensive `type(mod.Update) == function` check in `Core.lua:Tick()` to prevent runtime nil-method Lua errors on any module.

### Release v2.6.6-azs
- **Minimap Boss & Chest Radar Restored**:
  - Fixed span transformation typo and decoupled phase detection from initial chest table presence.
  - Added support for both AZS_LAIRS and AZS_GetLairs(), accurately mapping awake/asleep states and remaining respawn countdowns.
  - Active bosses/guardians rendered prominently in high-visibility Neon Crimson with HIGH frame strata.
  - Removed internal model purging in Minimap.lua, ensuring player blips and 3D scenes remain crisp and intact.
- **Dynamic Combat Text & Floating Damage Restore**:
  - Blizzard standard floating combat damage numbers (CombatDamage, CombatLogPeriodicSpells, SHOW_COMBAT_TEXT) are no longer permanently locked to zero.

  - Seamless sync across Options, slash commands (/bw combattext), and login events.

- **Cross-Platform Numeric Class Resolution:** Added `CLASS_ID_MAP` (1=Warrior, 2=Paladin, 3=Hunter, 4=Rogue, 5=Priest, 7=Shaman, 8=Mage, 9=Warlock, 11=Druid) in `ResolveClassColor` and `GetClassColor`.

  - Quick toggle between compact merged view and detailed separated view anytime.

- **Stock Level-Up Icon Suppressed**: Automatically hides the default engine level-up button (via \hudLevels = 0\ and \AZS_SetHudShown('levels', false)\) so only our custom, non-obtrusive Cyberpunk Level-Up button is shown.

# KeijinUI 4.7.0

## English

* **Damage numbers fixed in the world:** With a game version that has the combat text feed (0.138 and later), the numbers of your hits, including those of companions, summons and totems, now come directly from the game. * **Clocks:** The minimap clock shows the client's local time, the time zone setting is gone. The game's local time clock below the minimap can be hidden in Settings, Minimap, "Show game clock (local time)", if the game version supports it.

* **Ability icons:** If the spell book returns only the game's question mark as an icon (for example for Rockbiter Weapon), KeijinUI now shows the correct symbol instead, including for timers and damage numbers.

# KeijinUI 4.6.1

## English

* **Damage reduction label:** the run value formerly labelled Armor is now called Damage reduction in the character window and character stats, matching what it does. The character window rows are slightly wider; where the full name does not fit, a short form is shown there ("DMG reduction" in English, "Réd. dégâts" in French). - **Your numbers in a panel:** the run's stats in a panel of the same make as the others, on the left of the screen. Ten show at first.
- **Yours to choose:** a new **Stats panel** tab ticks each of the 22 stats on or off and gives each number one of 15 colors. It can also stay in sight while you choose cards (**Card choice**).

**Boss bars**
- **In the nameplates' look:** the name over the bar on the left, the plate's rounded bar in the kind's color, a white rim (gold on your target), a soft glow under the mouse, the share on the right and the boss's debuffs inside on the left.

**Nameplates**
- **Debuffs inside:** on elites, guardians and bosses, our debuffs in small icons inside the bar, from left to right. A guardian's and a boss's come from the game, with their stacks; an elite's show while it is your target or under the mouse, as the game shares no elite's. Off with **Debuffs inside the plates** (Nameplates).

**Minimap**
- **On the move:** an awake guardian's skull follows the guardian, blinking orange, and goes back to its lair once it is slain. Each boss gets a horned skull that goes where it goes, the final boss in an orange glow. Elites can get a bone skull too (off). The Minimap tab: **Lairs follow their guardian**, **Bosses** and **Elites**.

**Unit frames**
- **Your shields:** striped light blue on your health bar, as in Survivor UI, and your health numbers count them too, in light blue, the share going past 100%. Off with **Shields on your health** (Unit frames).

**Also**
- **Jewelry:** a piece with many effects takes as many lines as it needs, each effect whole; it used to be cut in the middle and cover the piece below.
- **Damage meter:** a new install no longer folds the small lines into Others.
…

**New nameplates in the old plates' manner, each enemy's kind told by the game itself, a beam of light over each cache, and a loot list.**

**Nameplates**
- **A new look:** a thin bar in a black line with round ends, the name over it and the health's share small inside. The rank and file in red; elites in green, lair guardians in blue, bosses in purple and the final boss in orange, each a little larger.
- **A skull over the name:** a plain bone one over an elite, the lairs' skull over a guardian, and an infernal one over a boss.
- **Told by the game:** the game's world anchors (its 0.139.2) say which plate is an elite, a guardian or a boss, so a lair guardian and its zone's elites, who share a name, each get their own color.
- **In a crowd:** the bosses' plates in front, then the guardians', then the elites'; the rank and file a little faded behind them, your target never.
- **Lines and light:** your target lined in gold, the enemy whose boss bar is under the mouse in white, and the plate under the mouse glows and comes to the front.
- **Friends:** your party in their class's color, pets, summons and totems in mint, thinner, in a gold rim.
- **What shows:** each kind on its own in the options: Normal monsters, Elite monsters, Guardians and Bosses. By default the elites, guardians and bosses show and the rank and file don't. "Your target, whatever its kind" shows your target's plate though its kind is off. A Boss bar switch there too, and the friendly plates are turned on once.
- An awake guardian's lair mark gives way to its nameplate while the plate shows.

**World markers**
- **Light beams over caches:** a column of gold light over each cache, its bag floating near the top. It is drawn over the world, so it fades where you stand in front of it.

**Loot list** (new)
…

**Marks on the world itself with the game's 0.139.2, two new Guide pages, Haste and Speed, and the interface keeps the size you chose.**

**World markers** (a new tab in the options)
- **Friends down:** in a co-op run, a gold cross over a friend who is down, with their name and how far.
- **Caches:** the minimap's loot bag over each cache still there, and how far.
- **Lairs:** the minimap's skull and the guardian's name over its lair while it sleeps. Awake, they follow the guardian out of its lair; slain, they go back over the lair with the time until the guardian comes back.
- **Arrows:** for friends down, caches and lairs out of sight, an arrow on a ring round you toward the nearest few, with how far.
- **Explosive orbs:** in a run with the Explosive affix, a pulsing mark over each orb.

**The Guide**
- **Haste:** every cooldown bonus is added into one number, and every wait is divided by 1 plus it. The game shows Haste as how much sooner, so its 50% already means twice as many spells, and 75% four times as many. There is no cap, but no spell comes back faster than 0.25 sec. **Echo** has no cap either: past 100% every spell strikes twice and the rest is the chance of a third, and each strike is a whole cast, aiming again and rolling its own Crit. Sliders for both, a spell's casts a minute in marbles, and the strikes of one cast.
- **Speed:** Speed stops at +120%, 15.4 yards a second. Pickup bonuses multiply each other, so two give more than their sum. Area widens every radius and reach: +100% doubles the radius and covers four times the ground.

**Fixed**
- **The interface's size:** the game puts its own UI scale back a moment after the world loads, so SurvivorUI Classic came back larger than the size picked in its options. It now keeps your size.
- **Haste's tooltip** on the character page: no spell comes back faster than 0.25 sec. It said each spell had a floor of its own.
…

**Two new Guide pages on your gear, Marks and Sets, and the level's cards come clean.**

**The Guide**
- **Marks:** what each star of a piece costs, rarity by rarity, and what all 8 pieces cost to 3 and to 5 stars. **Other classes done** sets how many of your other classes have that set done: each takes 5% off, up to 40%, as the game counts it. The three stars that open something on a set are there too, and hovering Empowered shows what it does for your class.
- **Sets:** every class's six sets, their 4-piece and 8-piece bonuses with the numbers, and the zones each one drops in. Pick a class, opened on yours, and the stars: 4 pieces, 8 pieces or Empowered. The part of each set those stars give lights up, and at Empowered the numbers that grow turn gold. Each set's name wears its color, as an item's does in a tooltip.

**The level's cards**
- **Hidden while you choose a card:** on a small screen the game's cards are large, and the run tracker, the build list, the jewelry and the damage meter stood on them. They now hide while you choose a card or a new piece of jewelry, and come back after.
- **Your pick of what stays:** a new **Card choice** tab in the options has **Hide everything while choosing cards**, and under it a box for each of the four. Untick the first for the four as before.
- **A note, once:** the first time you wait in town or at **Move to begin**, a box says so, with **Keep it hidden**, **Show as before** and **Choose pieces**.

SurvivorUI Classic is a branch of [Survivor UI](https://github.com/morderous/survivor-ui) in the game's own look. It works on its own: neither addon needs the other.

## Install
…

**A switch for the cooldown text, exact crits on the build list, a damage meter that scrolls and a clock your way.**

**New**
- **Cooldown text is your choice:** **Cooldown text on the action bar**, in the options' Action bar tab, turns the numbers on the buttons on or off, with the dark over them.
- **The damage meter scrolls:** with more to show than the lines you set, a scroll bar comes up at its right: drag it, click it or use the wheel, so the meter can stay short. Only the small lines fold into Others now: the rest no longer go there for lack of room.
- **Your time, your way:** hover the clock under the minimap to see what a click does: it opens the options' Minimap tab, with **Your computer's time** to tick, or untick for a slider to any time zone you want, and **24-hour clock** to tick for 24 hours or untick for 12. The game's clock has neither, so a clock of this addon takes its place, in the same spot, only when you ask for what it cannot show.

**The game's new data**
- **Each hit where it belongs** (the game's 0.139): the game now says which meter line each hit counts toward, so a proc that borrows a spell, like Flametongue Weapon's Fire Nova, no longer adds to that spell's crits on the build list, and Survivor UI's numbers name it right.
- **Talent icons in every language:** with the game in another language, a talent's line on the damage meter shows its icon and its tag.
- **The minimap's pins follow you live** (the game's 0.132), in dungeons and raids too. They used to jump about once a second.
- **The new Enhancement Shaman** (the game's 0.134 to 0.137): the new talents and Rockbiter Weapon have their icons, and Call of Flame is out, as the Shaman no longer has that spell.

**The Guide**
- **A word from the Guide:** the first time you play with this version, a small card beside the Guide's button says it is there. It shows once, and never again.
…

**Introducing the Guide.** A new button on the minimap opens a window of pages that explain how the game's numbers really work, in plain words, with colors, sliders to try and your own hero's numbers. Every number in it was read from the game's executable (game version 0.131). It's an ongoing project: more pages are coming, and feedback is welcome.

**The Guide**
- **The button:** on the minimap's rim, in our own art: a gold ! while there is a page to read, a ? once all are read. Hide it on the options' Minimap tab; `/suic guide` opens the Guide too.
- **Luck:** the bag of marbles, the magic number, and sliders for Luck and level that fill a bag of 100 marbles.
- **Damage:** the four boxes of a hit, what is added and what multiplies, and where buffs like Battle Shout go, each with its tooltip.
- **Crit:** why Crit stops at 100%, where the rest goes, and three cards that show which +10 is worth most for your hero right now.
- **DoTs:** a clear warning that Crit and Crit Dmg do nothing for them, when a DoT's damage is set, how copies grow with your level, and marbles for the ticks.
- **Not DoTs:** the spells that look like DoTs and aren't, one by one with a tooltip: Consecration, Flamestrike, Blizzard, Rain of Fire, Hurricane, Volley, the traps and Hellfire. They crit, and two on the ground at once both count.
- **Reduction:** how Damage Reduction works, its 60% cap, the talents that touch the cap, the talents of every class that add to the number, each on its class's color with a tooltip, and a bar to try it on.

**Also new**
- **Character panel tab** in the options: use the old page, no changes, or ours. It moved here from General, and with the old one chosen the hero no longer turns by dragging.
- **Build list:** the spells stand by rank, the highest first.

SurvivorUI Classic is a branch of [Survivor UI](https://github.com/morderous/survivor-ui) in the game's own look. It works on its own: neither addon needs the other.

## Install
…

**A very classy new character panel.** The character page is rebuilt from the ground up, and the rest of the interface gets a long list of small comforts.

**The character panel**
- **One panel for everything:** a wider window in the look of the other panels, the hero in the middle, the item slots at both sides. The game's Run Stats box is folded in, so every number lives in one place. The Character, Skills and Honor tabs and the ammo slot are gone.
- **Turn your hero:** hold the mouse on the hero and pull. This works on the game's own page too.
- **Main stats:** Damage in green, Crit Dmg and Crit in orange, since those two work as a pair. Hover one for its formula, read from the game's code, with your own numbers in it: what your level, gear and the rest add, your average hit, and what your damage, crits and haste give together.
- **Luck:** your odds of a legendary (orange), epic (purple) or rare (blue) on Cards (spell cards, rings and trinkets) and on Neck (amulets). Hover it for the whole roll: each rarity's weight and share, what amulets, hoards and bosses add, and your odds of a legendary among a level-up's 3 cards.
- **Four small panels** under the hero, by kind: Bonus, Utility, Defense and Offense, with the game's own numbers and tooltips. Haste shows its formula on its tooltip, and Armor now reads Dmg Reduction, first in Defense.
- **Your name in your class's color,** a shaman's blue, in the damage meter too, and **a new ring round the portrait,** our own art, sharp at any size.
- **The character page in one panel**, on the options' General tab, brings the game's own page back.

**Combat**
…

SurvivorUI Classic is a branch of [Survivor UI](https://github.com/morderous/survivor-ui) in the game's own look. It works on its own: neither addon needs the other.

## Changes

- **Combat text off:** Show the combat text, on the options' Combat text tab, turns it all off at once: the numbers and words over the enemies and everything over your hero. It keeps from one game to the next.

## Install

**With the launcher:** download `SurvivorUI-Installer.zip` below, unzip it and open `SurvivorInstaller.exe`. On a PC with no launcher before it, it installs SurvivorUI Classic and Survivor UI by itself once the game is there. If you already have a launcher, in the **Addons** tab pick **SurvivorUI Classic** and click **Install**. A new version then comes by itself once the game is closed, unless you untick **Auto Update when ready**.

**By hand:** unzip `SurvivorUIClassic-0.2.4.zip` into `benilla-config\AddOns\`, so you have `AddOns\SurvivorUIClassic`, then restart the game.

SurvivorUI Classic is a branch of [Survivor UI](https://github.com/morderous/survivor-ui) in the game's own look. It works on its own: neither addon needs the other.

## Changes

- **Restart game:** with the Survivor UI launcher open (1.7.1 or newer), Quit game in the Change UI panel becomes Restart game: the game closes and the launcher opens it again by itself. Without the launcher it stays Quit game.
- **Nothing through the level's cards:** the action bar, the summons and the talent cooldowns fade while the cards are up, as the game could draw an icon of theirs over a card (seen with Survivor UI).
- **Change UI:** a button under the options' tabs, there on every tab, in place of Switch to Survivor UI on the General tab, opens the panel that picks the interface. With Survivor UI turned off in the game's Options, AddOns tab the button still shows, and the panel says where to turn it on.
- **The chat's place through a change of interface:** the game keeps one place and size for the chat, so Survivor UI's stayed on after coming back. SurvivorUI Classic now keeps its own and puts them back as it starts; with none kept yet and the chat where Survivor UI left it, the chat goes back to the game's first place.
- **Reset on the damage meter:** the arrow beside the fold button starts Damage Done and DPS over from that moment, each spell's damage, damage a second and share counted from there, as Survivor UI's Reset. The Healing, Boss Damage and Party pages stay the game's. A new run starts the meter over by itself.

## Install

**With the launcher:** download `SurvivorUI-Installer.zip` below, unzip it, open `SurvivorInstaller.exe`, and in the **Addons** tab pick **SurvivorUI Classic** and click **Install** (installed from there already: **Update all**).

**By hand:** unzip `SurvivorUIClassic-0.2.3.zip` into `benilla-config\AddOns\`, so you have `AddOns\SurvivorUIClassic`, then restart the game.

Addon package for **SurvivorsDragonUi 3.2.96**.

## Install

1. Download [SurvivorsDragonUi.zip](https://github.com/migwynkriid13/SurvivorsDragonUi/releases/latest/download/SurvivorsDragonUi.zip) from the latest release.
2. In the game, open **Options → AddOns → Open AddOns Folder**.
3. Extract the ZIP and put the `SurvivorsDragonUi` folder there.
4. Enable the addon and enter a run. Type `/sdui` to set it up.

For a manual Windows install, open the folder containing `AzerothSurvivors.exe` and place the addon in `benilla-config/AddOns/`. The finished path should be:

```text
benilla-config/AddOns/SurvivorsDragonUi/SurvivorsDragonUi.toc
```

**Optional Windows auto-update:** Download [avrt.dll](https://github.com/migwynkriid13/SurvivorsDragonUi/releases/latest/download/avrt.dll) and place it beside `AzerothSurvivors.exe`. It updates the addon before the game starts. If checking or downloading fails or takes more than 10 seconds, the game starts with your installed copy. Enable the addon in **Options → AddOns**.

Remove `avrt.dll` to stop automatic updates. It cannot be used alongside another mod that needs the same filename. See [details and troubleshooting](updater/README.md).

**Playing in a browser?** Open **Options → AddOns → install a .zip** and choose the downloaded ZIP.

<details>
<summary>Windows settings and older installations</summary>

The game keeps addons, addon data, options, key bindings, chat windows and camera settings in `benilla-config` beside `AzerothSurvivors.exe`. On the first launch after this folder change, it copies addons and settings from older folders, keeping newer changes and filling in missing settings. Characters are unaffected.

</details>

Pendant of the Plague's explosions no longer end up in an "Other hits" row under Devouring Plague.

Description:

# Azeroth Cursor 1.2.0 — Optional Class Icons

Show your class crest on the cursor — or keep the ring alone. Marker and icon are
independent. Thanks to **Joker / Kohrinthian** for the class masks in
[PR #2](https://github.com/Maidenquinn/AzerothCursor/pull/2)!

## Optional class icon

- Toggle **Class icon** / **Icône de classe** (**off by default**).
- Use the icon alone, the ring marker alone, or both together.
- All nine classes, including Rogue / Voleur, as circular white masks that tint
  with your marker color.
- Dedicated **class icon size** slider (8–120).
- With the icon on, class-color buttons also choose which crest to display.

## Randomize and polish

- **Random** / **Aléatoire** (and `/azcursor random`): marker stays on; randomizes
  halo, class icon, sliders, color and icon token.
- Live cursor overlay while options are open.
- Preview keeps the same marker/icon proportions as the real cursor.
- Texture reload when switching class so preview and live stay in sync.

## Download and update

Download **AzerothCursor-1.2.0.zip** below. Close the game, replace the `AzerothCursor`
folder in your active `benilla-config/AddOns` directory, keep `AzerothCursorDB`, and restart.
Open the cyan minimap button or `/azcursor`.

Use the attached player ZIP rather than GitHub's automatic source archive.
Your saved settings and original-cursor default are preserved. No other addon is required.

## Validation

Native Lua 5.0.3 regression tests cover optional/independent class icons, all nine
masks, Random, preview proportions, FR/EN, class colors, scaled maps and persistence.
Runtime syntax, TOC/version consistency and all twenty TGA assets pass as well.

Tests simulate FrameXML behavior; keep an eye on native rendering after `/reload`.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/Maidenquinn/AzerothCursor/blob/v1.2.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/Maidenquinn/AzerothCursor/issues)

# Azeroth Cursor 1.0.0

Keep track of your mouse when the screen fills with spell effects in Azeroth Survivors.

## Features

- High-contrast cursor ring with black outline, adjustable size, thickness and opacity.
- Optional halo and animation, crosshair and center dot.
- Original, Balanced, Intense combat and Minimal presets with live preview.
- Sliders and +/- buttons. Editing a value enables the marker immediately.
- Color wheel, brightness control and RGB sliders. Cancel restores the previous color and enabled state.
- Draggable minimap shortcut, saved preferences and French/English options.
- Locate-cursor beacon with `/azcursor find`.

The native cursor stays unchanged on first installation. Effects activate when
you choose them; all marker overlays allow clicks through. No other addon is required.

## Installation

Download **AzerothCursor-1.0.0.zip**, close the game, and extract the
`AzerothCursor` folder into the active `benilla-config/AddOns` directory.
Enable the addon if needed and restart. Open the cyan minimap button or `/azcursor`.
Keep existing `AzerothCursorDB` when updating from a test build.

**Use the attached player ZIP, not GitHub's automatic source archive.**
The matching `.sha256` file lets you check the download.

The maintainer reported the final candidate working in game and authorized 1.0.
Standalone native Lua 5.0 tests cover behavior, settings, strict ColorSelect texture
arguments and regressions. They do not certify every native rendering path.

latest.notes:
Builds can now plan which cards to banish, and the Chronicle shows your co-op party at the press of a button. Co-op runs are counted correctly again, the best run goes by level, and the wishlist window keeps its size wherever you put it. Most of this came from player feedback, thank you!

⛔ Banish

* Every build has three banish places under its jewelry, in a small triangle. Click the + to choose: two lists, Spells and Jewelry.
* Any card can be banished, the build's own spells and the starting spell too: you keep the spell, but no more upgrades for it are offered, so the ones you want come more often (for example, a Magma Totem build banishing three of its other spells).
* In a run, the wishlist window shows the banished cards in a row under the build's card. The game does not tell addons which cards it offers or which you banished, so click an icon once you have banished it: it turns grey with a green tick. The marks start fresh every run.
* The Chronicle keeps each run's banish list with your marks ("Banish 2/3" on the build line, the cards on hovering it).
* Build codes carry the banish list. Older codes and older versions of Azerloot still work, without it.

🛠️ Builds

* The spell places are numbered 1 to 6, for the order to take them in.
* Battle traits in two columns, the page's rows evenly spaced, Strengths and weaknesses keep their five lines.
* Paladins, Shamans and Druids have a Relic place instead of Ranged.

📖 Chronicle

* Best run: survived first, then the higher level, then the longer time. Damage no longer decides, and your best runs are measured anew once.
* Co-op: going down no longer ends a run in the book. Before, a run was cut at your first fall and carried on as if in endless mode; such runs are repaired, and those that reached endless mode count as survived.

Scholomance has opened its doors: the new zone with its five bosses and the Tier 0.5 set of every class are in the book, with the set bonuses and the real numbers. The Chronicle lets you take a run out again, the Hunter's Kill Command and the new necklaces are in, and spell texts are read anew after the game's latest client.

📚 Scholomance

* The zone with its five bosses: Kirtonos the Herald, Ras Frostwhisper, Doctor Theolen Krastinov, Lord Alexei Barov and Darkmaster Gandling, each with its picture, a few words about it, its arrival time and health, its attacks and phases (Kirtonos' forms, Ras' Frost Armor, Gandling's Headmaster's Office, Class Dismissed, Pop Quiz and The Last Examination), and what to do about them.
* Boss warnings for the five, with their short names.

🛡️ Tier 0.5 sets

* All nine class sets (Heroism, Soulforge, Beastmaster, Darkmantle, Virtuous, Five Thunders, Sorcerer's, Deathmist, Feralheart): every piece with its picture, slot and stats as the game shows them, and the set bonuses at 4 pieces, 8 pieces at 3 stars and 8 pieces at 5 stars.

📖 Chronicle

* Remove a run: hover a run in the list and a small red x appears at its end. Click it twice within 3 seconds and the run is gone for good; the best run and all the records are found again among the runs left.
* The empty places of a run's spells and jewelry stay on the page, marked with a red x, so you see at a glance what was missing.
* Co-op: the hero who dealt the most damage stands next to the party's DPS, no hovering needed.

The Shaman's rework is in the book: Stormstrike, Rockbiter Weapon and the five new necklaces, with their real numbers. Plus Seal of the Damned's new ceiling and the game's latest texts in every language.

⚡ Shaman

* New spells: Stormstrike and Rockbiter Weapon, each with its picture, what it does and a line under its name. Call of Flame is gone.
* New necklaces, with their rank-1 numbers as the game has them:
  * Cinderheart Pendant (Fire Nova): +50% area, +25% damage, its hits stun for 1.5 sec.
  * Winter's Embrace (Frost Shock): slows by 70% for 6 sec, 75% more damage to already chilled enemies.
  * Earthshatter Seal (Earth Shock): 75% more damage to enemies below 35% health, a kill cuts its remaining cooldown by 50%.
  * Emberwake Pendant (Flame Shock): +40% damage, each tick also hits 2 nearby enemies within 6 yd for 50% damage.
  * Eye of the Tempest (Stormstrike): every fourth Stormstrike strikes again for 100% damage, with one more target at ranks 5 and 10.

* Builds: with Rockbiter Initiation a build can start with Rockbiter Weapon instead of Lightning Bolt. Shared build codes keep it.
* Your saved builds and older build codes simply drop Call of Flame and the necklaces that are gone, so their places are free again.

💍 Rings

* Seal of the Damned: 48% at Legendary (was 40%), and picked again it grows toward 100% (was 40%).

🌍 Languages

* The new spells, necklaces and their lines in the game's own words in German, French, Spanish and Portuguese.
* Tooltips are read in every game language again after the latest updates: the Enhancement talents, the necklaces' target ranks, Pact of the Nathrezim, the Dwarf's and Human's new racials, and more.

⬆️ Updating
…

Your wishlist no longer hides behind the level-up cards, the Chronicle remembers each Heroic run's affixes, and every spell text matches the game's latest update.

📋 Wishlist window

* The wishlist window (the tracker) now stays on top of the game's level-up and jewelry cards, so you can still see what you're hunting for while you pick. This uses the game's new addon function from 0.126; older game versions simply keep the old behaviour.

📜 Chronicle

* Heroic runs now keep their affixes, shown beside the level: "Zul'Gurub · Heroic III: Sanguine, Explosive · …". If the line gets too long for the page, hover it: the tooltip names the Heroic level and what each affix does.

🌍 Languages

* All of the game's texts are read anew, so spell tooltips in German, French, Spanish and every other game language are recognised again after the latest changes: Soul Link (now up to 10% of your max health), Improved Demoralizing Shout (now for your allies too), and the new texts for Heroic, the armory and co-op.

* By hand: download `Azerloot-2.5.5.zip` below (not "Source code") and unpack it into `benilla-config\AddOns`, beside `AzerothSurvivors.exe`. It holds one folder, `Azerloot`, which replaces your old one. Your builds, wishlist, collection, chronicle and settings are kept.

Ready for Heroic: the book now knows which boss mechanics only Heroic brings, its numbers say they are Normal's, and the Chronicle remembers the Heroic level of every run. Plus a fix for class amulets shown under the wrong spell.

⚔️ Boss pages

* Boss towers and gazes now only come on Heroic, with the "Old mechanics" twist. Their attacks say so: "Only on Heroic with Old mechanics." This affects Lord Aliden Perenolde, Hakkar, Sapphiron and Kel'Thuzad.
* Bloodlord Mandokir's Threatening Gaze is back on his page, as a Heroic-only attack.

📜 Chronicle

Le gestionnaire se lit dans l'ordre profil, addon, onglet, section, réglage. Les trois apparences restent au choix. Les profils ne copient pas les collections ni l'activation des addons.

### Limites
Tous les réglages ne sont pas importés. Le suivi des sorts d'Azerloot est exclu des profils. Un rechargement nécessaire est signalé, jamais lancé automatiquement.
